treatment.logline: Inside a rain-bound cash van, a personal recording gives way to a work directive; Dinu's glance at his wrist precedes a change of route without explaining his allegiance.

arc.beat: Establish the sealed working world and the private photograph.
Let the recording register before the incoming contact changes the pressure.
A glance at the thread, then a practical steering movement.

treatment.approach: A roughly ninety-second pool of essential interior coverage, with restrained handheld observation rather than exterior spectacle. Hold the listener instead of visualizing either remote person. Establish the dashboard phone before playback, keep the photograph in its original place, and reserve the final emphasis for the wrist glance and actual turn. Longer coverage sustains pauses and offers clean listening faces; recordings are never repeated in the intended sound edit.

treatment.geography: Camera stays within the front cabin. Dinu occupies the right-hand driver's seat; wet roadway is ahead, dashboard photograph is left of the instrument cluster, and a fixed phone is farther left angled toward him. Choose a plain dark work shirt, right hand at the wheel's upper-right quadrant and left hand at its lower-left quadrant. The red thread is on his left wrist. No handheld device operation while moving; playback and connection are automatic after the source is established.
treatment.key_image: The red thread on a resting steering hand shares the frame with Dinu's lowered eyes before those eyes return to the road.
advice: Use source-identifying phone screens before either remote audio begins; final screen lettering can be composited.
Do not repeat L3 or L5 when using overlapping listener coverage.
Keep road motion abstract through rain; no legible route signage or invented destination arrival.
The photograph is a worn, small dashboard object, not a portrait cutaway introducing the remote performer.

editor_notes: The 12 must takes total 88 seconds against a 90-second target. This is a raw-material total, not a finished runtime: dialogue takes overlap, and handles are inside the takes. Pace the intended scene with held driving and reactions without replaying either line.

A is the passenger-side cabin master; B and E are the matching three-quarter and near-frontal listener views; C keeps the photograph in the cabin; D establishes the mounted phone and its changing status; F holds Dinu's face and left wrist together.

L3 and L5 are each recorded separately and added once in post, device-filtered from the fixed phone. All picture takes remain vocally silent. Add rain, engine, wipers, ringtone and playback/connection sounds in post as appropriate; no music is planned.

For b6, the F shot carries the wrist glance and return of the eyes; the A shot carries the subsequent steering movement. Match forward gaze, both hands, left-wrist thread, road movement and intermittent sodium light at the cut.

The phone is an implied device fixed to the dashboard, farther left than the photograph; playback and hands-free connection require no hand movement. Composite the caller ID Mudalali and phone interfaces in post for reliable legibility. Keep the faded photo fixed; its tiny figures are static and indistinct, never an animated remote performer.

The packet did not specify Dinu's clothes, the wrist side or the precise dashboard positions. The consistent staging choices are a plain dark work shirt, thread on the left wrist, photograph left of the instrument cluster, and mounted phone farther left.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not requested effects in the intended cut; the held clean sources can support them if the editor chooses. No slow motion is planned.
Avoid mirror views, rapid finger interaction, body contact and sharply rendered crowds. Do not invent an arrival, signage, an explanation of the thread, or new dialogue.

editor_notes: The 12 must takes total 88 seconds against a 90-second target. This is a raw-material total, not a finished runtime: dialogue takes overlap, and handles are inside the takes. Pace the intended scene with held driving and reactions without replaying either line.

A is the passenger-side cabin master; B and E are the matching three-quarter and near-frontal listener views; C keeps the photograph in the cabin; D establishes the mounted phone and its changing status; F holds Dinu's face and left wrist together.

L3 and L5 are each recorded separately and added once in post, device-filtered from the fixed phone. All picture takes remain vocally silent. Add rain, engine, wipers, ringtone and playback/connection sounds in post as appropriate; no music is planned.

For b6, the F shot carries the wrist glance and return of the eyes; the A shot carries the subsequent steering movement. Match forward gaze, both hands, left-wrist thread, road movement and intermittent sodium light at the cut.

The phone is an implied device fixed to the dashboard, farther left than the photograph; playback and hands-free connection require no hand movement. Composite the caller ID Mudalali and phone interfaces in post for reliable legibility. Keep the faded photo fixed; its tiny figures are static and indistinct, never an animated remote performer.

The packet did not specify Dinu's clothes, the wrist side or the precise dashboard positions. The consistent staging choices are a plain dark work shirt, thread on the left wrist, photograph left of the instrument cluster, and mounted phone farther left.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options, not requested effects in the intended cut; the held clean sources can support them if the editor chooses. No slow motion is planned.
Avoid mirror views, rapid finger interaction, body contact and sharply rendered crowds. Do not invent an arrival, signage, an explanation of the thread, or new dialogue.
blend_notes: c13: Cut into c11 after Dinu lowers his gaze and return before he looks up; carry c11's cabin ambience, with no dialogue.
c14: Cut into c08 as the incoming contact appears, then return to Dinu; carry c08's incoming alert and cabin ambience.
c15: Lay a selected portion over Mudalali's L5 audio from c09 or c10, retaining the essential listening face elsewhere; do not repeat the directive.
c16: Lay the near-profile reaction over Aruni's L3 audio from c05 or c07; use only one continuous playback of the recording.
c17: Open immediately before c01, carrying c01's rain and engine ambience into the master; no dialogue.
c18: Close after the completed turn in c12, carrying c12's rain, engine and tire wash; no dialogue.

review.why: The thread insert punctuates the private glance, and the interior forward view lets the new heading settle after the turn.
The mounted-phone insert isolates the incoming contact and sharpens the interruption.
The held steering grip provides a controlled physical counterpoint under the directive without anticipating the turn.
A tight near-profile hold gives the editor a more intimate listening detail under the personal recording.
Rain-lit windshield texture opens the journey from inside the cabin, retaining the contained visual approach.
The existing dashboard-level composition already makes the photograph prominent while retaining Dinu; another insert would dilute that deliberate framing.
The existing master clearly establishes the fixed playback source before the recording; a separate phone shot would duplicate its purpose.
